parts.name: Central Connector (Vertical)
parts.description: Steel spring-loaded central connector, vertical orientation, that makes a 90 degree hidden connection where profile ends are captivated; the mounting profile must be milled for it.
features: 90 degree, hidden connection used when profile ends are captivated

parts.name: Milling Connector
parts.description: Steel milling connector in bright finish that installs with no machining required; connectors can be used in pairs.
features: Connector can be used in pairs
parts.dimension_notes: D = length of the connector body (the drawing measures it to the E screw head, not past it); B and E are the thread/screw sizes called out on the drawing

parts.name: T-Matic Connector
parts.description: Steel T-Matic connector in silver with a left-handed threaded barrel and a self-retained M6 x 40mm SHCS; installs with no machining and allows infinite positioning.
features: Left-handed barrel thread and self-retained screw to support ease of installation
parts.dimension_notes: E = barrel thread (left-handed threads), F = self-retained screw; A is measured from behind the head to the barrel end, not the overall length

corrected: 14132: dimension_notes 'D = overall length; B and E are the screw/thread sizes called out on the drawing' -> 'D = length of the connector body (the drawing measures it to the E screw head, not past it); B and E are the thread/screw sizes called out on the drawing'

14197: dimension_notes 'A = overall length, E = barrel thread (left-handed threads), F = retained screw' -> 'E = barrel thread (left-handed threads), F = self-retained screw; A is measured from behind the head to the barrel end, not the overall length'
remaining_doubts: 13201 is printed as '13201*'; the asterisk is a footnote marker (corner clearance notch, page 11-27), so part_number is kept as '13201' and the footnote is in notes.
Central Connector required machining (Central Connector Profile Milling, ref. page 11-21) has no service number on page 4-20, so no machining_service part was created.

3960 (RT) Ready Tube bolt assemblies are recorded in notes, not suggested_hardware, because only 15/F hardware rows go in suggested_hardware; the plates carry an RT badge, so a downstream merge might want 3960 as structured hardware.
